  "situation": "On 12 April 1999 a NATO aircraft released two laser‑guided bombs at a railway bridge in eastern Serbia. A passenger train was crossing the bridge at the moment the first bomb struck, killing at least ten people and injuring at least fifteen. The bridge was identified as a legitimate military objective linked to a supply route for Serb forces in Kosovo. The pilot or weapons systems officer saw the train only moments before impact and could not abort the first bomb; a second bomb was released at a different point on the bridge and also struck the train. The committee reviewing the incident concluded that the bridge was a lawful target and that the train was not deliberately targeted, but it was divided on whether the second strike involved recklessness. The committee applied its criteria for initiating an investigation and determined that those criteria were not met.",
